about: The tractus of the formulary “First Sunday of Lent” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Whoever lives with the help of the Most High will remain under the protection of the God of heaven. He will say to the Lord: “You are my support and my refuge, my God; I will hope in Him. For He Himself has freed me from the hunters’ snare and from the harsh word.” He will shade you with His shoulders, and under His wings you will hope. His truth will shield you on every side: you will not fear the terror of night, the arrow flying by day, the trouble that roams in darkness, or ruin and the demon at midday. A thousand will fall at your side and ten thousand at your right, but it will not come near you. For He has commanded His angels to guard you in all your ways. They will carry you in their hands so that you never strike your foot against a stone. You will walk over an asp and a basilisk, and you will trample a lion and a dragon. “Because he has hoped in Me, I will free him; I will protect him, because he has come to know My name. He will call on Me, and I will answer him; I am with him in distress. I will rescue him and glorify him; I will satisfy him with a long life and show him My salvation.”
